title: How Yahia Bakour grew context.dev: listen on calls, build what customers ask, bootstrap first
summary: Yahia Bakour, founder of context.dev (a web data API for AI agents, YC-backed), explains how a simple brand-data API grew into scraping and entity data by following customer asks. He covers product-led growth curves, discovery calls where he mostly listens, ignoring competitors, and when to raise versus bootstrap.

principles.text: Start simple and become infrastructure; repeated customer asks tell you what to build next.
principles.quote: if three people ask for the same thing and they're all paying you, it might be worth it.

principles.text: Product-led growth is slow, then compounds as you pass repeated critical-mass thresholds. Persist through the slow months.
principles.quote: the amount we grew in the first year, we grew in the next 3 months, and then the amount we grew in the first year and 3 months, we grew in the next 1 month.

principles.text: Growth came from being very active on X, SEO kicking in, and a product good enough to cross the usability threshold.
principles.quote: we became extremely active on X. We became extremely extremely active online. Our SEO kind of kicked in on the keywords that we were looking for.

principles.text: On customer calls, stay quiet and have them walk through their workflows; spot patterns, then pitch features they didn't know they needed.
principles.quote: first half of a call, you just shut up and be quiet and listen to people.

principles.text: Don't watch competitors; once you break through the noise, build only from what customers ask for.
principles.quote: we don't look at what competitors are doing. I I definitely try not to. And then we only build off what customers ask

principles.text: Bootstrap if you can; raise to accelerate when you see huge potential, not for prestige.
principles.quote: raising money is not an accomplishment. It's just a necessary part of the process.
